title: Quasi-isomorphism of the concrete scalar-extension unit on a ringed Cech model
statement: Let C be a small site, phi:R -> B a morphism of commutative ring sheaves, and I a locally finite type ideal subsheaf [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-ideal, def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Assume B is R-flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and R/I -> B/IB is an isomorphism. Let epsilon:K -> R[0] have the local extended Cech description [def-weil-pbc-local-extended-cech-description]. Form scalar extension by the actual degreewise sheafified sectionwise tensor B tensor_R K [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with its unit u:K -> r(B tensor_R K) given by x -> 1 tensor x; r is restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Then this specified unit is a quasi-isomorphism. The module also constructs its augmentation to B[0] and proves compatibility with epsilon and phi on complexes. No derived completeness of any object or equivalence of categories is assumed.

source.place: Tags 099H and 099I, the termwise scalar-extension comparison in the construction of K prime.

proof.text: The module constructs the scalar-extension functor explicitly by sheafifying the sectionwise tensors and their maps. The unit sends x to 1 tensor x followed by sheafification, and its naturality is proved from sheafification naturality. Tensor adjunction and the sheafification hom equivalence construct the lifted coefficient map; composing with the unit recovers the original linear map. Apply this to phi on the rank-one module and then to complexes concentrated in degree zero, obtaining the augmentation and its proved compatibility. Thus all data below are these specified constructions, not arbitrary witnesses.

Flatness makes tensoring exact: apply it to the kernel/image short exact sequences of each differential. It therefore preserves quasi-isomorphisms and transports the given derived local description of K.

Restrict to a slice with a finite generating list for I. Restriction is exact and preserves quotients, and flatness restricts. Identify tensor of localization with localization of B by b tensor (a/f^n) -> b phi(a)/phi(f)^n and its inverse b/phi(f)^n -> b tensor (1/f^n). These commute with differentials and augmentations; finite products are finite sums. Apply flat extended Cech comparison to deduce that u is a quasi-isomorphism on this slice.

Local finite generation gives a covering by these generating slices. The kernel and cokernel cohomology sheaves vanish on that cover and hence globally, so u is a quasi-isomorphism. The augmentation equation already holds on complexes. For I zero the empty tensor Cech model is the ring complex, and the quotient hypothesis makes the coefficient map an isomorphism; for I the unit ideal both models are contractible.

lean.statement:
theorem flat_ringed_cech_base_change_unit_quasiIso
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    {R B : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} (φ : R ⟶ B) (I : RingedSiteIdeal R)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u} (siteModuleRings R))]
    [∀ U : C, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (ringedSiteModules.{u} (siteModuleRings (R.over U)))]
    (hI : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} I.module)
    (hflat : SheafOfModules.IsFlat
      ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).map φ)).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit (siteModuleRings B))))
    (hquot : I.IsQuotientIso φ)
    (K : ringedSiteComplex R) (ε : K ⟶ ringedSiteRingComplex R)
    (hK : HasLocalExtendedCechDescription R I.module I.inclusion K ε) :
    QuasiIso (siteExtendScalarsComplexUnit φ K)

split_report.summary: Constructed scalar extension, its additive functor structure, units, tensor-adjoint lifting, and the augmented complex compatibility explicitly. The remaining strictly smaller assertion is quasi-isomorphy of the specified scalar-extension unit; the augmented-model existence theorem is proved from it.
